candidates.angle: user topic: no-Origin client under every CORSAllowedOrigins value; removed behaviour; twin input paths
candidates.summary: a node whose cors_allowed_origins is narrowed refuses /websocket to every client that sends no Origin header, the in-tree Go WS client included, while it still serves the same client's HTTP POST
candidates.failure_scenario: Operator sets cors_allowed_origins = ["https://gno.land"] (or ["https://*.gno.land"]). node.go:951-953 hands that list to NewWebsocketManager, which installs rs/cors OriginAllowed as CheckOrigin; OriginAllowed lower-cases the empty Origin and finds it in no list (rs/cors v1.11.1 cors.go:462-480), so gorilla answers 403. rpcclient.NewWSClient (ws.NewClient dials with a nil header) fails with 'unable to dial RPC, websocket: bad handshake', so tx-archive backup over ws and gnohealth timestamp over ws stop working against that node, as do curl, websocat and Node ws clients; an HTTP POST with no Origin to the same node still answers 200. At the merge base every row connects. Under nil and ["*"] the no-Origin client still connects. A browser cannot omit Origin on a WebSocket handshake, so accepting an absent Origin keeps the CSWSH protection.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-2-no-origin-client_test.go tm2/pkg/bft/rpc/lib/server/zz_solo_finder_2_no_origin_test.go && go test -count=1 -v -run TestSoloFinder2_NoOriginClient ./tm2/pkg/bft/rpc/lib/server/ : the two narrowed rows fail at head; with the origins argument dropped (merge base, via go test -overlay) all four rows pass
candidates.evidence: head dd05df75b: cors_allowed_origins=["https://gno.land"] HTTP POST=200 ws.NewClient err=unable to dial RPC, websocket: bad handshake; ["https://*.gno.land"] HTTP POST=200 ws.NewClient err=unable to dial RPC, websocket: bad handshake; [] and ["*"] err=<nil>. Merge base d25b308c1 (overlay, constructor without origins): all four rows err=<nil>, PASS.

candidates.summary: gnodev hot reload stops working for a page opened at the documented http://localhost:8888, since the injected script dials ws://127.0.0.1:8888/_events and the new same-origin default refuses it
candidates.failure_scenario: Default gnodev: -web-listener 127.0.0.1:8888, and app.go:492 builds the hot-reload target from that string, so hotreload.js dials ws://127.0.0.1:8888/_events. docs/resources/gnodev.md:39, docs/builders/quickstart.md:22, docs/builders/getting-started.md:198 and contribs/gnodev/README.md:16 tell users to open http://localhost:8888. The browser then sends Origin: http://localhost:8888 with Host: 127.0.0.1:8888; with CheckOrigin nil, gorilla's checkSameOrigin compares the two host strings and answers 403. The page never reloads on save, and nothing outside the browser console says why. Any -web-listener string differing from the host the user types (0.0.0.0, a LAN IP, a hostname) fails the same way. At the merge base the upgrade succeeds.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/solo-finder-2-gnodev-page-origin_test.go contribs/gnodev/pkg/emitter/zz_solo_finder_2_origin_test.go && (cd contribs/gnodev && go test -count=1 -v -run TestSoloFinder2_PageOrigin ./pkg/emitter/) : localhost row 403 at head, 101 at the merge base
candidates.evidence: head dd05df75b: page http://127.0.0.1:35051 dials ws://127.0.0.1:35051/_events: status=101; page http://localhost:35051 dials ws://127.0.0.1:35051/_events: status=403, FAIL. Merge base d25b308c1 (same file via go test -overlay): both rows status=101, PASS.
